The move could help eligible claimants complete Russian legal, administrative and DNA formalities.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday said the right to seek compensation must be enforced and asked the Ministry of External Affairs to consider issuing a public notice inviting the families of Indians who died while fighting in the Russia-Ukraine war to seek assistance and compensation.
The ministry told a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that 51 Indians who fought in the war had died, while 77 recruits remained untraced.
The court also reviewed efforts to identify and repatriate mortal remains, secure compensation and help the affected families complete legal and administrative formalities.
The court asked the ministry to file a fresh status report specifying the compensation paid by the Russian government to six families whose members died in the war zone.

Five claims had been settled fully and one partially.
The bench said the right to seek compensation was available to the families of all 51 people who had died.
It asked the District Legal Services.
Authorities of Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh to comply with its earlier direction to provide free legal aid to the families.
The assistance is to cover the submission of claims, DNA tests and other legal and administrative formalities that the families are required to complete.

stories.headline: LAC must be stable for normalisation of ties with China: Jaishankar
stories.title: LAC must be stable for normalisation of ties with China: Jaishankar
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14: The Line of Actual Control (LAC) has to be stable for normalising relations between India and China, External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said, asserting that any disturbance along the border will have consequences. Jaishankar also linked expansion of trade and investment ties between the two countries to peace and tranquillity along the border. "The point we make to the Chinese is: 'If you want a normal relationship, if the rest of the relationship is to move, it's common sense -- It is a no-brainer that the boundary has to be stable and that we need peace and tranquillity in the border areas'," he said. Jaishankar, speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum on Tuesday evening, noted that the situation along the LAC has "settled down" to a great extent since 2024 and that the relationship is "commensurately moving towards normalcy." In the last few months, both sides have rolled out a series of confidence-building measures to repair ties frayed by the more than four-and-a-half-year military standoff in eastern Ladakh. The face-off ended in late 2024. To a question on whether India would allow more Chinese investment in the country in case there was an "early harvest" agreement on the boundary question, Jaishankar broadly said that various possibilities are being looked at. "We are now looking at those possibilities, and we have to see where we go. But we are not insisting that you have to solve the boundary issue in order to do business." "What we are saying is: the bar is lower. The bar is: maintain peace and tranquillity. I wouldn't link the early harvest to anything other than the boundary question resolution. Anything we do on any policy we have on business, market access issues will be dealt with separately." The external affairs minister also flagged concerns over economic issues with China. "We also have very major economic issues with China. If you look today at the trade balance, it is completely tilted (towards China)," he said. "The tilt is extremely one-sided, and in many sectors where we have done well with the rest of the world, we have not had market access; we have not had a successful business operation for that sector in China," he said. "We do believe today that we're not getting a level playing field in China in the manner in which we have given a level playing field to them," he noted. Jaishankar also referred to the Galwan valley clashes of 2020 and explained how it brought the ties under severe strain. "From 1975 till 2020, a good 45 years, no blood was shed on that border. The last time there were fatalities was in 1975. In this period, India-China relations did grow," he said. "Then in 2020, when we were in the midst of the Covid lockdown, we had a series of border issues, and it culminated in a clash in which a number of soldiers were killed on either side," he said. "For us, what it represented was a very profound departure from the situation that was prevailing since 1975. If the peace and tranquillity in the border areas are disturbed, then the relationship will have consequences," he said. Jaishankar said those consequences were very visible in the next few years until peace and tranquillity was restored.

stories.headline: DRI busts illegal import of over 73,00,000 kg of Pakistan-origin rock salt; 4 arrested
stories.title: DRI busts illegal import of over 73,00,000 kg of Pakistan-origin rock salt; 4 arrested
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) has once again unearthed a large-scale scheme to circumvent India’s prohibition on the import of goods originating in or exported from Pakistan under “Operation Deep Manifest”. DRI detected the import of 295 containers carrying 7,311 metric tonnes of Pakistan-origin Industrial/Himalayan Rock Salt, with an estimated market value of around Rs. 30 crore. The consignments were routed through Colombo Port, Sri Lanka, and falsifying their origin by using fabricated certificates of origin and invoices issued by UAE-based entities. Acting on specific intelligence, DRI launched a coordinated, fortnight-long operation between 26 September and 11 October 2026, conducting searches at linked premises in Gandhidham, Adipur, Veraval, Panipat, Pune, Patiala, Delhi and Mumbai. Investigation revealed that nine importers had brought in the 295 containers through Mundra and Kandla ports since March 2026, in violation of the prohibition. Out of the total 295 containers detected, five containers carrying 140 MT of Industrial/Himalayan Rock Salt, valued at Rs. 24.41 lakh, have been seized at Kandla Port. In addition, sales proceeds amounting to Rs. 20.96 lakh held in the importers’ bank accounts have been seized. Preliminary investigation has uncovered a transnational network involving entities owned by Pakistani, UAE, Sri Lankan and Indian nationals. The network allegedly coordinated the shipments and supporting documentation to disguise the Pakistani origin of the goods. Fabricated invoices issued by Dubai-based firms were used to support the transactions. Significantly, Bills of Lading relating to the Pakistan–Sri Lanka leg of the shipments and customs declarations filed with Sri Lanka Customs expressly mentioned Pakistan as the country of origin and India as the final destination. The Certificates of Origin submitted by the importers were found to be fabricated. Four persons have been arrested under the provisions of the Customs Act, 1962: two proprietors/partners of importing firms, a Customs Broker’s G-card holder, and the owner of a Dubai-based supplier who had also established and operated an importing firm in his father’s name. In a similar crackdown last month, DRI seized over 362,000 kg of Pakistan-origin dry dates packed in 13 containers imported by a Mumbai-based firm at CFS Ambad, Nashik. These cases highlight the evolving methods used by transnational networks to circumvent India’s import prohibition on Pakistani origin goods through third-country routing, false declarations of origin, fabricated trade documents and opaque financial arrangements. DRI remains committed to identifying and dismantling such networks and safeguarding India’s economic and national security interests. Following the Pahalgam terror attack in April 2025, the Government of India imposed a complete prohibition on the direct or indirect import or transit of all goods originating in or exported from Pakistan, in the interest of national security and public policy, vide DGFT Notification No. 06/2025-26 dated 02.05.2025.

stories.headline: Sheikh Hasina calls Rahman’s BRICS Summit absence ‘counterproductive’
stories.title: Sheikh Hasina calls Rahman’s BRICS Summit absence ‘counterproductive’
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14 : Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's decision to skip the BRICS summit in India was "immature" and damaged Bangladesh's national interest, former premier Sheikh Hasina has said, warning that foreign policy driven by personal reactions or short-term political calculations is inherently counterproductive. In an exclusive interview with PTI, Hasina said Bangladesh's participation at the summit of the influential grouping could have opened up new opportunities for the country's economic and social development, but that chance was lost. The former Bangladesh prime minister said if her presence in New Delhi was the reason behind Rahman's refusal to attend the summit, it was very unfortunate, as relations between two countries cannot be determined by personal considerations or political sensitivities involving one individual. Questioning Rahman's decision, Hasina said that a responsible government should "open doors for the country, not close them." New Delhi had extended an invitation to Bangladesh Prime Minister Rahman for the BRICS summit in his role as the current chair of BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation). However, Rahman opted out of the summit, which took place in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. "It was deeply unfortunate that Bangladesh chose not to participate. In my view, it was an immature decision and one that did not serve Bangladesh's national interest," Hasina said. "BRICS is not simply a diplomatic gathering. It brings together major emerging economies and creates opportunities for cooperation in trade, investment, infrastructure, technology and development. By participating, Bangladesh could have gained valuable experience and opened new opportunities for its own economic and social development. That opportunity was lost," she said. The former prime minister said foreign policy cannot be conducted through personal reaction or short-term political calculation. "India is our closest neighbour and an important historic partner, but BRICS engagement is also about Bangladesh's own place in the international community," she noted. The 78-year-old Hasina, living in Delhi since she left Bangladesh following the collapse of her government in August, 2024 in the face of a massive anti-government agitation, also recalled, how then prime minister Ziaur Rahman visited New Delhi in 1979 even when she was staying in India. "After the assassination of the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, along with members of my family on August 15, 1975, and the killing of the four national leaders inside Dhaka Central Jail on November 3, Ziaur Rahman came to power through an unconstitutional process," Hasina said in response to written questions. "Yet when he visited Delhi in 1979, I was living in Delhi. When he travelled to London in 1980, I was also in London. My presence in either city did not prevent him from travelling there," she said. "So why should my presence in Delhi prevent Ziaur Rahman's son, Tarique Rahman, from coming to India today? What is the real reason behind such a decision," she asked. "Relations between two countries cannot be determined by personal considerations or political sensitivities involving one individual," she stressed. Hasina also highlighted how her government's foreign policy approach helped Bangladesh's economic growth. "During my tenure, we maintained strong relations with India while also expanding cooperation with China, Russia, Japan, the United States, Europe and many other partners," she said. "Friendship with one country never required hostility towards another. Bangladesh needs a mature, balanced and confident foreign policy. A responsible government should open doors for the country, not close them," she said. The India-Bangladesh relations came under some fresh strain after Hasina held a virtual media interaction in New Delhi on August 5. Following the event, Dhaka reiterated its demand for her extradition and even sought to link it with Rahman's planned trip to India. New Delhi sought to distance itself from the event, saying it neither played a role in it nor endorsed Hasina's comments. The former prime minister also attacked the Rahman government for its overall foreign policy direction, and said it should be "independent, balanced and guided by national interest." "The principle given by the Father of the Nation, Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman, remains the best guide: friendship to all, malice to none. India is Bangladesh's closest neighbour and historic friend from the Liberation War," she said. "China is also an important development partner. Japan, the United States, Europe, ASEAN and the Muslim world are all important to Bangladesh. The problem is not engagement with China or any other country. The problem begins when one relationship is used against another," she said. "It begins when anti-India rhetoric is encouraged for domestic politics. It begins when major decisions are taken without transparency," she added. The Awami League leader said Bangladesh is passing through a "grave national crisis as democratic space has been "closed". "The judiciary has been used for political revenge. Media freedom has been restricted. Law and order have weakened. Minorities feel unsafe. Extremist forces have regained space. The economy has suffered," she said. "This is no longer only an Awami League issue. It is a national crisis. One of the country's largest political forces has been banned. Its leaders are in jail or forced into hiding," she said. "Millions of its supporters have been denied normal political rights. A country cannot return to stability by excluding such a large section of its own people. The suffering is being felt across the country, but Awami League leaders, workers and supporters have faced an unprecedented burden of political persecution," she said. Hasina, without divulging specific details of her return to Bangladesh, said she is going back to restore democracy. "Thousands have been jailed, many more have been forced into hiding, and families have lost homes, jobs, businesses and livelihoods simply because of their political identity," she said. "My return is part of the struggle to restore democracy, voting rights and the rule of law. I want to stand beside the people of Bangladesh, fight for their rights, and help restore democracy, security and development in my country," she said. "The people of Bangladesh must be allowed to decide their own future through a free, fair and inclusive election. That is why my return will be significant. It will be a step towards returning Bangladesh to its people," she added. At the same time, she admitted that her return to Bangladesh could be risky as she was given a death sentence by a Bangladeshi court, but asserted that she was not afraid. "This is not the first time death has come close. In 1975, my father, mother, brothers and almost my entire family were murdered. In 1981, despite military rule and intimidation, I returned to Bangladesh. There have been repeated assassination attempts, including the August 21, 2004 grenade attack, as well as imprisonment, conspiracy and political persecution," the Awami League leader said. "The greater concern today is not personal safety. It is the destruction of justice in Bangladesh. A death sentence imposed through a politically motivated process, without a genuine opportunity to defend oneself, cannot be called justice," she said. PTI

stories.headline: India sees no problem in any agreements with US: Piyush Goyal
stories.title: India sees no problem in any agreements with US: Piyush Goyal
stories.summary: India does not see any problems in its agreements with the United States, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on Wednesday, playing down any suggestion that ties depend on who occupies the White House.Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Goyal was asked whether relations would improve after the tenure of the current US president. He said they were already “very good”. “I don’t see any problem in any agreements with the United States. It’s about trade, defence partnership, technology partnership, it’s our critical maintenance partnership and our people-to-people engagement,” he said, adding that Washington is India’s largest trading partner and will remain so in the years ahead.The relationship, Goyal said, will strengthen “irrespective of changes in political thinking” in either country. Drawing on economic, political and security imperatives, it is “a very safe relationship” that the rest of the world need not worry about, he added.Also Read: India-US trade talks hit a plateau as FM flags tough road ahead“I think the US and India have a very consequential relationship, and it’s only going to get better, irrespective of changes in political thinking, whether in India or in the US,” the commerce minister said further.Goyal said the pandemic exposed India’s vulnerability when critical supplies, including vaccines, failed to arrive. stories.headline: India’s wholesale price inflation reaches 11.39% in September
stories.title: India’s wholesale price inflation reaches 11.39% in September
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 14 : India's wholesale price inflation (WPI) came in at 11.39 per cent in September against 9.92 per cent in August amid higher prices of fuel, crude petroleum, food articles and several manufactured products, according to provisional data released by the government on Wednesday. According to the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) for all commodities was at 112.5 in September from 110.8 in August. However, the government said the final WPI for July remained unchanged at an index level of 110.0 with annual inflation also unchanged at 9.78 per cent. Among major categories, inflation in primary articles stood at 8.67 per cent from 7.76 per cent a month earlier, while fuel and power inflation climbed to 25.85 per cent from 22.93 per cent, the ministry said. Inflation in manufactured products -- which carry the highest weight in the index -- was at 9.76 per cent. The ministry said major contributors to wholesale inflation during September included mineral oils, food articles, crude petroleum and natural gas, coal and lignite, basic metals, chemicals and chemical products, textiles, rubber and plastic products and electrical equipment. In addition, the WPI Food Index recorded annual inflation of 8.66 per cent in September compared with 7.05 per cent in August. Within the fuel basket, inflation in mineral oils stood at 40.02 per cent, while crude petroleum and natural gas recorded inflation of 57.32 per cent year-on-year. Fuel and power prices overall rose to an index level of 110.5 in September from 108.3 in August, according to the official data. Separately, the Output Producer Price Index (PPI) for all commodities rose to 112.5 in September from 110.8 in August. Additionally, the trial Input Producer Price Index (IPPI) for the manufacturing sector increased to 106.1 in September from 104.2 in August. The final index of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of July 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 98.97 per cent, the ministry said. "The provisional index of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of September 2026 has been compiled with a weighted response rate of 83.4 per cent," it added, Notably, the government will release WPI, Output PPI and trial Input PPI data for October on November 16. --IANS

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today advanced the date of hearing in Delhi SIR matter, after it was alleged that voters, whose names have been deleted pursuant to the SIR exercise, are being asked to fill Form 6 for re-inclusion of their names on the electoral roll.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi advanced the hearing date from October 30 to October 28, on hearing Advocate Prashant Bhushan.

When Bhushan urged that a hearing on October 28 might not make much of a difference as October 30 is the last date for correction of deletions, the CJI said, "we are thinking of passing an order that will take care of [all this]".
Bhushan was mentioning the application filed by transparency activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri in the pending petition against Delhi SIR.
"They are asking people to fill up Form 6.
But Form 6 has a declaration that they have never voted before.
If they give false declaration, they are liable to imprisonment.
We are seeking direction that ECI allow them to fill up Form 8, which is for shifted voters, or create some other Form", he submitted.
He prayed that the matter be listed on Friday.
Ultimately, the bench posted the main matter on October 28.

The main petition alleges failure on the part of the Election Commission of India (ECI) and the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer to adequately disclose the names of voters issued notices and the specific reasons for issuing them.

The petition, also filed by Anjali Bhardwaj and Amrita Johri, seeks disclosure of the criteria, definitions, algorithmic parameters and operational guidelines governing the classification of voters under the category of 'Logical Discrepancies'.

stories.headline: Lieutenant Governor congratulates GMC Srinagar on Advancing Internal Medicine Conference
stories.title: Lieutenant Governor congratulates GMC Srinagar on Advancing Internal Medicine Conference
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 14: The Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha today congratulated Government Medical College, Srinagar for organising a conference on “Advancing Internal Medicine: From Evidence to Excellence in Clinical Practice”. In his message, the Lieutenant Governor underscored the critical role of internal medicine in delivering holistic and patient-centric healthcare. The Lieutenant Governor said that physicians often face the challenging task of identifying complex underlying health conditions from seemingly simple symptoms. He noted that the strength of internal medicine lies in its ability to view the human body as an interconnected system and to understand the complete medical story of a patient through clinical knowledge, experience and careful observation. The Lieutenant Governor also stated that observation, reason, human understanding and courage remain the defining qualities of a physician. He highlighted that physicians frequently serve as the first point of medical contact for families and, in many cases, build enduring relationships across generations, rooted in trust, compassion and scientific evidence. The Lieutenant Governor in his message lauded Government Medical College, Srinagar for its significant contribution to medical education and healthcare, noting that generations of doctors trained by the institution continue to serve across Jammu Kashmir and the country. The Lieutenant Governor also highlighted the emerging healthcare challenges. “While infectious diseases remain a concern, lifestyle-related disorders such as diabetes, hypertension, obesity, fatty liver disease and cardiovascular ailments are assuming epidemic proportions. We need to ensure that advances in diagnostics, therapeutics and medical technologies reach physicians and patients in rural and remote areas as effectively as they do in urban centres,” he said. The Lieutenant Governor also called upon the medical fraternity to strengthen indigenous research and generate evidence relevant to India’s diverse population. He said that the country’s demographic diversity, combined with the expertise and commitment of doctors, presents immense opportunities for scientific discovery and innovation. “Medical science is making historic advances, and new drugs and diagnostic tools have opened up new possibilities for treatment. The greatest need today is to ensure that these innovations are not available only to physicians in large cities, but also reach doctors in villages. We must ensure that there is not even the slightest gap between urban and rural areas in access to facilities and available tools. This should be the first objective of this conference,” he said. The Lieutenant Governor also outlined a five-year roadmap and proposed six key commitments for the medical community including expanding access to advanced medical knowledge through digital health platforms and telemedicine, prioritising preventive healthcare and early detection of diseases, using technology and artificial intelligence as supportive tools while preserving clinical judgement, continuously strengthening research capacity, ensuring the wellbeing of doctors and addressing professional burnout and preserving human compassion at the centre of healthcare delivery. The Lieutenant Governor also urged the young doctors to remain curious, embrace innovation and learn from experienced mentors. He also called upon senior physicians to generously share their clinical wisdom and guide the next generation of healthcare professionals. “Early detection of diabetes, hypertension and liver disease is less costly and can help reduce treatment expenses. I urge all physicians and internists to lead prevention campaigns at the community level, because a doctor’s voice can have an extraordinary influence on society. I have every confidence that people will take your advice seriously when it comes to preventing lifestyle-related diseases. We must value physicians’ hard work, service and dedication. Along with caring for patients, hospitals and institutions, it should be ensured that doctors are cared for too. Providing them with better workplaces and working conditions should be a priority,” the Lieutenant Governor said.

stories.headline: IMD update: N-E monsoon to arrive tomorrow, heavy rain lashes Tamil Nadu coast
stories.title: IMD update: N-E monsoon to arrive tomorrow, heavy rain lashes Tamil Nadu coast
stories.summary: Isolated very heavy rain likely over Kerala and Mahe, and Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Thursday and heavy rain across several southern and adjoining regions over following five days
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The keenly-awaited north-east monsoon could set in over the South Peninsula on Thursday, with piloting moderate to heavy rain already lashing parts of the Tamil Nadu coast through Wednesday, and thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds signalling a gathering change in weather over the past few days.
India Meteorological Department (IMD) expects the onset of the October-December rainy season to coincide with withdrawal of preceding south-west monsoon.

Driving the transition is a cyclonic circulation over the Comorin area, about 1.5 km above the surface, linked to a trough stretching from the Gulf of Mannar across the south-west Bay of Bengal to the Odisha coast.
By Wednesday afternoon, the trough extended along the coasts of Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, ready to channel moisture-laden easterlies from the Bay towards the South Peninsula.
The IMD has forecast isolated very heavy rain over Kerala and Mahe, and Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Thursday.
Heavy rain is may persist across several southern and adjoining regions over the following five days, with thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds adding to the unsettled conditions.
Strong surface winds are also forecast over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema from Thursday.

The North-East monsoon is set to announce arrival over Tamil Nadu in a deceptively subtle fashion, not with a well-defined storm spinning over the Bay of Bengal, but with an elongated trough in the easterlies that may organise clouds and trigger rain gradually over the larger South Peninsula as well.

This will hold true for the island nation of Sri Lanka just to the south-east, which has come out with outlook for heavy rain not just for Thursday but following days also along its east and south-east coast that open out to the south-west Bay.
The Sri Lanka Meteorological Department said a ‘low-level atmospheric disturbance persisting in the Bay may bring cloudy skies and increased rainfall over the island.
Showers or thundershowers will occur at times in the Northern, Eastern, Southern and Western provinces.
Heavy falls above 7.5 cm are likely at some places in Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central and North-central provinces and in Trincomalee and Kurunegala districts.
